newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Potential EMU founders list lengthens.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Potential EMU founders list lengthens.

text.p: Europe's single currency union is almost certain to be launched on schedule and the list of potential founder members is lengthening, according to a survey of leading European forecasters.

The poll, conducted by international economic survey firm Consensus Economics Inc, showed that Germany, France, the Netherlands and Belgium were unanimous choices as core members of European economic and monetary union (EMU).
But more than 70 percent of the forecasters expected Austria, Ireland and Finland to be founder members as well.
Support for Finland has rocketed to 76 percent since a similar survey five months ago. Then only 48 percent of the forecasters believed the Finnish markka would be a founder EMU member.
Some 96 percent of the 78 experts said they expected EMU to hit its target launch date of January 1, 1999.
Luxembourg, widely tipped by most experts to be a founder EMU member, was not included in the survey.
Countries expected to join in the three years following the launch are, in descending order of probability, Italy, Sweden, Britain and Greece, the survey showed.
The poll said the flexible wording of the Maastricht Treaty, which set the rules for EMU entry, was bolstering the chances of countries whose economies were not shaping up to the guidelines.
"Given that a number of other countries will either meet, or come close enough to meeting, the other criteria, the list of potential EMU entrants has continued to lengthen," it said.

"Finland's entry in the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), coupled with a significant improvement in its budget deficit outlook, has produced a sharp increase in the number of forecasters expecting it to join EMU from the start."

A Reuters survey of predictions by European analysts published last week showed an 83 percent chance of a single currency being launched on time, with a core group of six countries -- Austria, Belgium, France, Germany, Luxembourg and the Netherlands.
